_: Notebook performance budgets, enforced by tools/notebook_perf_budgets.py (bytes from the Vite manifest; latency from a tools/notebook_scale_benchmark.py --json report). EDITED BY HAND, and only when a budget is raised or lowered ON PURPOSE: say why in docs/notebook/perf-budgets.md and in the commit. Never regenerate this file from a run -- a budget that follows the measurement is not a budget.

search.why: The brief's search budget: what a member waits for when the Notebook list answers a search, a filter or the switcher, at 50k notes. Local gate (the 50k seed is too slow for CI).

reads.why: Lane I's own budget, not the brief's: the whole-library reads the sidebar and ticker surfaces make on open, held to the same line as search.

tasks.why: Lane I's own budget, not the brief's, and ABOVE the 100 ms search line on purpose: the tasks view parses every task-bearing note's body in Python (~3.8k notes, ~9 MB of JSON at 50k). The lever under it is a maintained task index, which is the every-writer aggregate the brief warned about; see perf-budgets.md section 2.

editor.why: The brief's editor budgets, measured in a real browser by tools/notebook_perf_harness.py (local only). The typing budget stops at 2,000 paragraphs: G-035's 71 ms/char at the size cap stands as the owner ruled.

search_ci.why: CI runs the 1k and 10k tiers only. At 10k the same line is loose on purpose: it catches the gross regressions (the correlated sidecar EXISTS was 717 ms p95 at 10k) without failing on a shared runner's noise.

reads_ci.why: The reads budget at the CI tier.

tasks_ci.why: The tasks budget at the CI tier.
